HTLV-1 represents a neglected retrovirus with a heterogeneous epidemiological distribution. This virus mainly affects closed or vulnerable populations and is prevalent in central-south Africa, the Andean region in South America, the Caribbean basin, and southern Japan. (4) HTLV-1 is mainly responsible for Adult T-cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL), a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by an aggressive disease course and poor responses to conventional therapies. (5) In addition, people living with HTLV-1 (PLwHTLV-1) can coincidentally develop cHL, as well as a variant of ATLL with morphological features indistinguishable from cHL, known as Hodgkin-like ATLL. (6–8) Strategies to differentiate cHL in PLwHTLV-1 from Hodgkin-like ATLL include: HTLV-1 basic leucine zipper factor in situ hybridization (HBZ-ISH), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in situ hybridization, assessment of PAX5, and demonstration of viral integration at the genomic level. (9) However, most of these techniques are not available in the global south, where both cHL and HTLV-1 are frequent. For instance, Peru has limited availability of these techniques despite its highest burden of HTLV-1-related complications in South America. (10) Consequently, in this study, we aimed to compare the clinical features and outcomes of PLwHTLV-1 diagnosed with cHL versus a propensity-matched group of cHL patients without HTLV-1 infection in a resource-constrained endemic country.

Oncogenic viruses are responsible for at least 10% of all malignancies worldwide with a disproportionate distribution affecting the global south. @schiller2021 Among them, Human T-cell Leukemia Virus Type 1 (HTLV-1) is directly responsible for Adult T-cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL), a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by an aggressive disease course and poor responses to conventional therapies. @matutes2018 In addition, HTLV-1 infection has also been linked to two largely indistinct Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL) entities: 1) classic HL (cHL) in patients living with HTLV-1 (PLwHTLV-1); and 2) Hodgkin-like ATLL. Characteristically, these two conditions develop similar morphological features, such as Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS)-like cells. However, Hodgkin-like ATLL has been described as an aggressive ATLL subtype with dismal outcomes, while the prognosis of cHL in PLwHTLV-1 has been suggested to be more favorable, though this remains controversial given its rarity and lack of real-world data. @niino2013 @bittencourt2010 @ohshima1997
